sections.label: Public transport and Changi Airport
sections.summary: In 2023 there were over seven million daily rides on public buses and trains, and Changi Airport served about 59 million passengers last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2023, we had over seven million daily rides on our public buses and trains, serving millions of commuters across the country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Last year, Changi Airport served about 59 million passengers.

sections.label: Port links and container throughput
sections.summary: The port is linked to 600 ports worldwide and in 2023 container throughput reached a new high of 39 million twenty-foot equivalent units.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our port is linked to 600 ports around the world and in 2023, our container throughput reached a new high of 39 million, 20-foot equivalent units.

sections.label: UK National Security and Investments Act
sections.summary: In 2021 the UK passed the National Security and Investments Act, allowing government intervention in certain acquisitions that could harm UK national security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2021, the United Kingdom (UK) passed the National Security and Investments Act, which allows the government to intervene in certain acquisitions made that could harm the UK's national security.

sections.label: Daily rides on buses and trains
sections.summary: Public buses and trains supported an average of 7.19 million rides per day in 2023, ferrying workers to and from their roles in the Singapore economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our public buses and trains supported an average of 7.19 million rides per day in 2023, ferrying our workers to and from their various roles contributing to the Singapore economy.

sections.label: Bill complements Significant Investments Review Act
sections.summary: According to MOT's press release, the Bill is intended to complement the Significant Investments Review Act, passed in January 2024 and effective 28 March 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to MOT’s press release, this Bill is intended to complement the Significant Investments Review Act, or SIRA, which was passed in January 2024 and came into effect on 28 March 2024.

sections.label: Taxi and ride-hailing daily trips
sections.summary: MRT and public bus operators are expected to be designated, while taxi and ride-hailing companies saw average daily trips rise 18.6% from 517,000 in 2020 to 613,000 in July 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While it is expected that our Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and public bus operators will be designated, what about taxi and ride-hailing companies which have seen their average number of daily trips increase 18.6% from 517,000 in 2020, to 613,000 in July 2023?

sections.label: Controller notification and approval thresholds
sections.summary: The Bill requires buyers into designated entities to notify the authority after becoming a 5% controller and to obtain prior approval before becoming a 25%, 50% or 75% controller.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, the Bill requires buyers into designated entities to notify the relevant authority after becoming a 5% controller, and to obtain prior approval of the relevant authority before becoming a 25%, 50% or 75% controller.

sections.label: Reconciling new and traditional powers
sections.summary: The passage asks how the new powers should be reconciled with those traditionally deployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How should we reconcile these new powers with those that we have traditionally deployed?

sections.label: Penalties for designated entities and transport operators
sections.summary: The passage compares maximum penalties for designated entities and bus and MRT service providers and asks whether penalties incentivise compliance and for consultation details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the maximum penalties for non-compliance for designated entities under the CAAS Act and the MPA Act range from $500,000 to $1 million, or a three-month imprisonment, the maximum penalties for equivalent offences for our bus and MRT service providers is a fine up to $50,000 or up to six months’ imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This difference appears to be deliberate so my question for the Minister is whether the penalties are significant enough to incentivise compliance without being overly burdensome for the operators?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share some further details on the scope and status of the consultation and agreement?

sections.label: Amendments to four transport legislations
sections.summary: The Bill provides for amendments in four key legislations relating to air, sea and land transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bill provides for the amendments in four key legislations relating to air, sea and land transport legislations, namely the Bus Services Industry Act 2015, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore Act 2009, the Maritime and Port Authority of Act 1996 and the Rapid Transport Systems Act 1995.

sections.label: Special Administrative Orders for licensees
sections.summary: The Bill enables the Minister to issue a Special Administrative Order or other orders in relation to a bus service licensee or a railway licensee if satisfied that conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Part 1, section 33D and Part 4A, section 27C of the Bill enables the Minister to issue a Special Administrative Order or other orders in relation to an entity who is a bus service licensee or a railway licensee, respectively, should the Minister be satisfied that one or more conditions be met.

sections.label: SIRA controls on designated entities
sections.summary: The recently passed SIRA empowered the Government to impose controls on the shareholders and management of designated entities' interests of national security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In fact, the recently passed SIRA empowered the Government to impose controls on the shareholders and management of designated entities' interests of national security.

sections.label: Designating Class 2 operating entities
sections.summary: Asks whether MOT or CAAS intends to designate the companies mentioned as Class 2 designated operating entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Apart from CAG, which will be designated as a Class 1 designated operating entity, does MOT or CAAS intend to designate the companies that the Minister has mentioned in his earlier speech as Class 2 designated operating entities?

sections.label: Seletar exclusion and maritime services
sections.summary: Asks if Seletar is excluded from the framework and notes clause 44 includes maritime services like bunker supply and salvage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Has Seletar been excluded from the designated entity framework because it only serves smaller aircraft or will the framework eventually be extended to Seletar as well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Likewise, for the maritime sector, clause 44 includes services, such as bunker supply and delivery, salvage operations and passenger ferry operations, in the definition of essential transport services.

sections.label: Offices for sector agencies
sections.summary: Asks whether similar offices will be set up in all sector agencies to implement the Bill's governance regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For the implementation of SIRA, an Office of Significant Investments Review (OSIR) was set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will there be similar offices set up to implement the requisite governance regime required by this Bill in all the different sector agencies involved?

sections.label: Support for transport Bill
sections.summary: States support for the Bill, which grants powers to ensure critical transport firms are properly led and operated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Not only are we a major aviation and maritime hub, our people depend on our world-class public transport network to get around and go to work to power our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I thus support this Bill, which grants the Government additional powers to ensure that critical transport firms are led by the right people and operated in a way that will maintain the stability of our transport system.

sections.label: Number of designated entities
sections.summary: Asks how many entities are expected to be designated as essential transport services under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How many entities do we expect to be designated as essential transport services under this Bill?

sections.label: Similar legislative regimes complexity
sections.summary: Notes the Bill mirrors the Significant Investments Review Act, creating five similar regimes and unnecessary complexity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many of the provisions in this Bill and the powers granted to MOT mirror those that are found in the Significant Investments Review Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This creates five very similar legislative regimes, resulting in unnecessary complexity in applying the individual statutes.

sections.label: Consistent approach for transport services
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government will ensure a consistent approach between critical transport services and significant investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will the Government ensure that we have a consistent approach between critical transport services and significant investments?

sections.label: New designated entities regime
sections.summary: The Bill proposes a new designated entities regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes a new designated entities regime.

sections.label: Clause 6 approval requirement
sections.summary: Clause 6 mandates prior written approval from LTA for actions like becoming a partner in a Class 1 operating licence holding partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, clause 6 of the Bill mandates prior written approval from LTA for seemingly basic actions like becoming a partner in a Class 1 operating licence holding partnership.

sections.label: Compliance costs of Bill
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government to provide a clear picture of the compliance costs associated with the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, it would be helpful if the Government could provide a clear picture of the compliance costs associated with this Bill.

sections.label: Minister for Transport intervention powers
sections.summary: The Bill grants the Minister for Transport broad powers to intervene in critical firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill grants the Minister for Transport broad powers to intervene in critical firms.

sections.label: Concerns on regime and competition
sections.summary: The passage raises concerns that the regime may deter investment, affect stock trading and efficiency, and calls for clarity on costs, competition and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed designated entities regime may impose bureaucratic hurdles and deter investment, potentially affecting stock trading and operational efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need clarity on compliance costs and timelines for approval processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, concerns arise regarding competition and consolidation within the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ensure that the Bill fosters healthy competition, preventing monopolies or duopolies that could stifle innovation and raise costs for consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Minister's broad powers require clear justification and accountability mechanisms to prevent misuse.

sections.label: Special Administration Order for transport failure
sections.summary: MOT is prepared to issue a Special Administration Order if a designated operating entity fails to provide essential transport services safely and reliably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thirdly, in the unfortunate event of a designated operating entity failing to provide essential transport services safely and reliably, we understand MOT stands prepared to issue a Special Administration Order.

sections.label: P2P platform passenger volume designation question
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MOT will consider designating platform providers as designated entities, citing P2P platforms serving over 180 million passengers a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, disruptions to such platform services could have far-reaching implications for those who rely on this means of transport for their daily commute or other purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I understand earlier from the Minister that the passenger volume at Changi Airport is about 59 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In contrast, the P2P platform serves more than 180 million passengers a year – about three times compared to passenger volume in Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, will MOT consider designating such platform providers as the designated entities?

sections.label: Similar legislation in other countries
sections.summary: Many other countries, including the US, UK, Australia and most EU members, have similar legislations with provisions on designation, ownership, management approvals and remedial directions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Many other countries, such as the US, the UK, Australia and most members of the EU, have similar legislations, including provisions regarding the designation of critical entities, ownership and operational controls, management appointment approvals, as well as remedial directions.

sections.label: Key entities providing essential transport services
sections.summary: Under the designated entities regime, the key entities are those involved in providing essential transport services in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the designated entities regime, the key entities are the ones involved in the provision of essential transport services in Singapore.

sections.label: Bill complements Significant Investments Review Act
sections.summary: The Ministry intends for this Bill to complement the Significant Investments Review Act, which scrutinises investments in entities critical to national security interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Ministry intends for this Bill to complement the Significant Investments Review Act (Sira) which scrutinises local and foreign investments in entities considered critical to our national security interests.

sections.label: Avoiding duplication with sectoral legislation
sections.summary: To avoid duplication, entities adequately regulated under sectoral legislation, including critical transport firms under MOT's sectoral Acts, are not intended to be designated under SIRA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To avoid duplication, we do not intend for entities adequately regulated under sectoral legislation, including critical transport firms covered under MOT’s sectoral Acts, to be designated under SIRA.

sections.label: Designated entities list timing
sections.summary: The initial list of entities will be designated by the end of this year, and companies not engaged so far are not currently planned for inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The initial list of entities will be designated by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If the relevant Authorities have not engaged your company on this Bill so far, it means there are currently no plans to include it as a designated entity.

sections.label: Equity interest holder requirements
sections.summary: Designated equity interest holders face less onerous requirements than designated operating entities, including no Special Administration Order and approval only for Chairperson and CEO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As designated equity interest holders are not direct providers of essential transport services, they will be subject to less onerous requirements than designated operating entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Designated equity interest holders will not be subject, for example, to a Special Administration Order, and will only need to seek approval for Chairperson and CEO but not the rest of their Board directors.

sections.label: Controls applied at entity level
sections.summary: Controls will be applied at the entity level even though the main focus is on parts of the business providing essential transport services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: While our main focus is with parts of the business related to the provision of essential transport services, the controls will have to be applied at the entity level.

sections.label: Step-in powers and Bill scope
sections.summary: Step-in powers are a last resort, and the Bill aims to strengthen transport sector resilience without interfering with day-to-day operations or commercial decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Step-in powers are a measure of last resort and, hence, before these powers are activated, it is likely that the authorities would already be in conversations with the entity to explore different ways to improve the situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This Bill will strengthen the resilience of our transport sectors in an increasingly complex operating landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proposed Bill does not change our long-standing position on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have, therefore, calibrated our controls to only what is necessary to enhance the resilience of our essential transport services and ensure that the requirements are not overly onerous to the companies and investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Bill does not interfere with the day-to-day operations of the entities or their commercial decisions, and bona fide approvals will be processed expeditiously.

sections.label: Government and Temasek ownership questions
sections.summary: The Member asked whether redundancies or divestment plans arise from the Bill given Government and Temasek ownership of covered companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Also, followed by that, I did ask the Minister whether, since some of these Class 1 bus licensees and other companies, SMRT, PSA Corp are owned by Temasek, and CAG is owned by the Government, are there some redundancies in any way arising from this Bill and whether or not there are any plans for divestment of the Government's stakes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I mentioned that the coverage includes companies that may be owned by Government, Temasek Holdings, but also other entities that may have other shareholders.

sections.label: Capabilities for extreme scenarios
sections.summary: Preparations for an extreme scenario require looking at capabilities to build up within LTA and the industry ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For the first question that Mr Tan asked, certainly, we would, as part of the preparations for an extreme scenario like this, have to look at where are the capabilities that we need to build up, not just within LTA, but also within the industry ecosystem as a whole.

sections.label: Tripartite collaboration fixing SMRT reliability
sections.summary: The approach is close collaboration with tripartite partners, as SMRT's reliability was fixed through LTA, SMRT and NTWU working together, not a Special Administration Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But as I clarified earlier, the approach that we want to take is actually to work in close collaboration with our tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, using SMRT as a good example, SMRT's reliability challenges were fixed and maintenance was improved, reliability improved, performance improved, not through the issuance of a Special Administration Order, but through the close collaborations among LTA, SMRT and NTWU, our union, working together, fixing the problems and it remains a continuous work in progress.
